title: Multiple Meanings of Get
focus: Diferenciar os vários sentidos dos phrasal verbs com get pelo contexto
verifiableTask: Interpretar e usar phrasal verbs com get em contextos diferentes e explicar cada sentido

content.text: get up · get on · get off · get over · get by · get along · get around · get away · get back · get through · get across · get at · get ahead · get behind · get out of · get round to (UK) / get around to (US).
Ao final da aula você consegue:
pelo contexto e usar os principais.
interpretar e usar phrasal verbs com get em contextos diferentes e explicar cada sentido.
What do you usually do to get away from stress?
We got away for the weekend.
I can't get over how beautiful it is!
We got through a tough year.
I got out of the meeting.
I never got around to calling him.
I couldn't get through to the bank.
I get on well with her.
We GOT aWAY for the weekend.
We got through a tough year, but we finally got away for a week.

explanations.general: Correct answer: What do you mean?
Correct answer: go somewhere to relax

questions.questionText: “I never got around to it” means…

options.text: I never found time to do it

explanations.general: Correct answer: I never found time to do it

questions.questionText: It's hard to get ______ on a small salary. (se virar — partícula)
“Get around to” is more American; “get round to” is common in British English.

content.text: I couldn't get through to customer service.
She got through a difficult divorce.
I can't get over how cheap it is!
He got out of washing the dishes.
If you want to get ______, you need new skills.
I'll get ______ to you by Friday.
→ got through / a tough exam period → got away / to the mountains → finally got around to / cleaning my closet

questions.questionText: “We got through three pizzas” — get through means…
“He got out of washing the dishes” means…

explanations.general: Correct answer: he avoided doing it

questions.questionText: I'll get ______ to you by Friday. (retornar — partícula)

explanations.general: Correct answer: make progress, be successful

questions.questionText: “I can't get over how beautiful it is” expresses surprise.
